definitions.explanation: First-person pronoun used mainly by males in casual or semi-formal settings.

examples.japanese: {僕|ぼく}は{学生|がくせい}です。
{僕|ぼく}の{名前|なまえ}は{田中|たなか}です。
{僕|ぼく}は{毎日|まいにち}{電車|でんしゃ}で{学校|がっこう}に{通|かよ}っている。
examples.english: I commute to school by train every day.

examples.japanese: {僕|ぼく}の{家|いえ}は{学校|がっこう}から{遠|とお}いので、{毎日|まいにち}{朝|あさ}{早|はや}く{起|お}きなければならない。
examples.english: My house is far from school, so I have to get up early every morning.

examples.japanese: {僕|ぼく}は{小|ちい}さい{時|とき}から{本|ほん}を{読|よ}むのが{好|す}きで、{毎週|まいしゅう}{図書館|としょかん}に{行|い}って{新|あたら}しい{本|ほん}を{借|か}りている。
examples.english: I've liked reading since I was little, and every week I go to the library and borrow new books.

notes:
{僕|ぼく} is a first-person pronoun used mainly by males.

USAGE:
- More casual than {私|わたし}
- Used by boys and men
- Common in everyday conversation
- Softer/gentler than {俺|おれ}

COMPARISON OF MALE PRONOUNS:
- {僕|ぼく}: casual, polite, soft
- {俺|おれ}: casual, masculine, rough
- {私|わたし}: formal, gender-neutral

Note: Young boys often use {僕|ぼく} when speaking to adults.
